title: DNA Extraction from Whatman Filter Papers
author: Xiang Guo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vjme4k6

steps.title: Place filter disc in tube
steps.instruction: Cut the blood‑containing Whatman filter paper disc and place it into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant repeatedly
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 5 min, discard the supernatant with a micropipettor, and repeat the centrifugation until a white or pink gel‑like DNA pellet forms at the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Measure nucleic‑acid absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 230 nm, 260 nm, and 280 nm; calculate the A260/A280 and A230/A260 ratios.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in Chelex
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 150 µL of 10 % Chelex‑100 solution (Merck MilliporeSigma, Catalog #C7901‑100G) and vortex briefly for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Heat at 100 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the Chelex‑resuspended sample at 100 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifuge post‑heat
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the heated sample at 20,000 × g for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add RNase‑free water
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL RNase‑free (DNAse/RNAse‑free) distilled water (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Catalog #10977023) and vortex to mix.

steps.title: Incubate at room temperature
steps.instruction: Incubate at 25 °C (room temperature) for 15 minutes to lyse residual red blood cells.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and store
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube with a micropipettor; proceed to downstream applications or store the DNA at –20 °C.
